keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

themes.name: LLM alignment, evaluation, and governance
themes.summary: These papers build detectors, monitors, benchmarks and conceptual frameworks for judging whether LLM behavior is safe, reliable and legitimate rather than merely accurate. Some probe internal representations or outputs to catch silent evidence loss, topic drift, bias, jailbreak susceptibility and unfaithful rationales, while others benchmark trustworthiness, contextual safety, judges and graders against human review. A further set argues about governance itself, proposing control-and-knowledge boundaries, participatory constitutions, justice frameworks and impossibility results for gatekeeping agents.

themes.name: Agentic LLMs, memory, and tool use
themes.summary: The papers study LLM agents and agentic systems that act through tools, environments, and memory across scientific, software, enterprise, and multimodal settings. They range from benchmarks of agent architectures and planning to memory and runtime mechanisms, and to applications in autonomous experimentation, design, and document or interface analysis.

themes.name: Robot foundation models and manipulation
themes.summary: These papers develop robot foundation models for manipulation: vision-language-action policies, dual-system and cross-embodiment manipulation frameworks, and policy learning from egocentric human video. They differ in whether they target representation and skill transfer across embodiments, efficiency and online adaptation of long-chunk action policies, or spatial grounding and task formulation in embodied vision-language models.

themes.name: Medical imaging and clinical reasoning
themes.summary: The papers span medical image analysis—segmentation, localization, registration, foundation-model adaptation, and fairness/interpretability—and clinical reasoning with language models, including evidence-grounded diagnosis, report evaluation, and surgical action reporting. They differ in whether they focus on imaging pipelines for detection and segmentation or on reasoning, evidence traceability, and reporting reliability in clinical decision support.

themes.name: Geospatial foundation models and reconstruction
themes.summary: The papers develop geospatial foundation models, embeddings, and reconstruction methods for remote sensing and spatial scenes. They differ by focusing either on unified perception and location representation or on reconstructing surfaces, driving scenes, and images from irregular, sparse, or specialized sensor data using triangulation, Gaussian splatting, depth guidance, and super-resolution pipelines.

themes.name: Time-series and tabular foundation models
themes.summary: These papers evaluate and adapt foundation models for tabular and time-series data, benchmarking tabular foundation models against tuned gradient boosting for churn and financial prediction, using in-context tabular models for causal mediation, and coupling time-series foundation models with LLMs or statistical refinement for forecasting. Others propose new architectures and evaluation protocols, including continuous-horizon forecasting, continuous-time set transformers, interpretable and change-point detection methods, and benchmarks for generalist tabular models and user event sequences. They differ in whether they benchmark existing foundation models, introduce new forecasting or representation architectures, or design evaluation settings.

themes.name: Reinforcement learning post-training
themes.summary: The papers apply reinforcement learning across diverse settings, from language-model post-training and distillation to control tasks such as meshing, flow control, traffic signals, and chemotherapy. They differ in whether they propose new training pipelines, reward-design and reward-correction methods, environments and benchmarks, or theoretical and efficiency analyses.

themes.name: Diffusion and flow matching generative models
themes.summary: The papers in this theme advance flow-based and diffusion-based generative modeling through theory, training and sampling improvements, and diverse applications. They range from a survey of geometric and stochastic foundations to distillation, robust flow matching, step-aware decoding, adaptive denoising, and manifold or physics-informed generative priors. Applications include image and video generation and restoration, compression, motion generation, planning and safety, inverse problems, seismic assessment, reinforcement learning, combinatorial optimization, and drug-design evaluation.

themes.name: Efficient LLM decoding and inference
themes.summary: The papers in this theme target the costs of serving and decoding large language models, spanning sparse-attention indexing, KV-cache and memory management, speculative drafting and verification scheduling, and communication or lookup-table placement for efficient inference. Others address sampling and uncertainty during decoding, tokenization and compression for cheaper inputs, and reproducible or vendor-guided deployment on specialized hardware. They differ in whether they attack attention latency, memory and communication bottlenecks, draft acceptance, or the decoding and sampling procedure itself.

themes.name: Multilingual and low-resource language modeling
themes.summary: The papers build benchmarks, datasets, segmenters, tokenizers, and evaluation protocols for languages and scripts that are underrepresented in mainstream language modeling, including Brazilian Portuguese, Thai, Indic languages, Hindi, Chinese, and mixed-script Uzbek. They differ in whether they measure tokenizer disparity and adapt byte-level or multi-word tokenization, create cultural, political-media, or educational resources, or address linguistic segmentation, OCR correction, historical script classification, and stylometric attribution.

themes.name: Federated learning and private inference
themes.summary: The papers cover federated learning variants—rank-heterogeneous LoRA fine-tuning, personalized federated reinforcement learning, Byzantine-robust aggregation, and verifier-pool collaboration across heterogeneous model families—alongside privacy-preserving inference and re-identification work such as homomorphic-encryption secure transformer inference, differentially private ranking inference, and privacy-aware top-view person re-identification. They differ in whether collaboration happens through shared parameters or shared verifiers, in how client heterogeneity and adversarial behavior are handled, and in whether privacy is achieved through encryption, differential privacy, or privacy-aware sensing.

themes.name: Speech and audio processing
themes.summary: The papers cover speech enhancement SDKs, codec-robust audio deepfake detection, spoken language diarization diagnostics, code-mixed speech recognition adaptation, spatial audio representation, a unified speech-and-audio foundation model, and full-duplex dialogue decisions. They differ in emphasis, ranging from streaming enhancement and robust recognition to audio-language understanding and diagnostic metrics.

highlights.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
highlights.why: The profit- and calibration-aware re-evaluation overturns the prior claim that TFMs decisively beat GBDTs on churn, showing nuanced significance only on some datasets after tuning, which tempers current TFM hype.
highlights.key_result: With a split-aware test and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparisons, TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more EMP than the best tuned GBDT on Cell2Cell (1.9%) and Iranian (7.6%), and these two gains also hold against each of the three tuned GBDTs separately; on Orange it is ahead in all 10 splits (14.3%), but the gain is not significant after correction (Holm p = 0.155).

On Orange it is ahead in all 10 splits (14.3%), but the gain is not significant after correction (Holm p = 0.155).

highlights.title: How Much of Your VLA Is kNN
highlights.authors: Denis Grachev, Damien LaRocque, Omar Moured
highlights.why: The kNN retrieval baseline achieves 91.7% on LIBERO and LAC tracks when fine-tuning merely improves keys, questioning whether VLAs generalize beyond demonstrations and suggesting a cheap baseline for evaluation.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks achieves a success rate of 91.7 on LIBERO without policy training, and under LIBERO-Plus perturbations retrieval shows the smallest drop of all evaluated policies; fine-tuning mostly makes the vision-language backbone a better retrieval key, and the actions of the VLA remain close to the demonstrations.
evidence: In this work, we show that retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks achieves a success rate of 91.7 on LIBERO without policy training. Under LIBERO-Plus perturbations, retrieval shows the smallest drop of all evaluated policies.
Across nine publicly available VLA, fine-tuning mostly makes the vision-language backbone a better retrieval key, and the actions of the VLA remain close to the demonstrations.

On average, the ResNet variant achieves a success rate of 88.7 on LIBERO and 75.5 on LIBERO-Plus. The multimodal variant reaches 91.7 and 82.4 , respectively, while the LAC key variant reaches 93.0 and 81.7 .

highlights.title: ExpertCrowd-SWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Expert-Authored Engineering Tasks in Unfamiliar Codebases
highlights.authors: Josip Vrdoljak, Akash Singh, Bas Steunebrink et al.
highlights.theme: Agentic LLMs, memory, and tool use
highlights.why: ExpertCrowd-SWE provides expert-authored, calibrated, partially credit-grading tasks in unfamiliar codebases, giving a more realistic frontier-agent benchmark than synthetic or familiar repos.
highlights.key_result: On EC-SWE, seven current models span 35 points and fall into four statistically distinct tiers; Claude Opus 5.5 (67.3%) and GPT-6 Astra (63.7%) lead without a statistically significant gap. No task is fully solved by every model, and on 80 tasks no model earns full credit on all five runs.

highlights.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
highlights.authors: Yikun Zhang, Minghao Guo, Guangxue Xu et al.
highlights.why: ProTEUS learns a mutation-resolved world model with fast physically valid structure prediction and closed-loop feedback, surpassing established models and enabling efficient exploration of combinatorial protein space.
highlights.key_result: ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type.
evidence: ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type.

highlights.title: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents
highlights.why: The impossibility theorem formally proves no finite, checkable rulebook can certify every safe program, providing a foundational limit for AI gatekeepers.
highlights.key_result: We prove that two rulebooks, one listing what is allowed and one listing what is not, cannot both be complete if every rule must be backed by evidence that a machine can check in finite time: checkable evidence can only establish what a finite record settles, and ``never'' and ``eventually'' are never settled by a finite record. For prohibitions the failure is one-sided—every violation can be caught by watching, but no safe program can be cleared for good—and for confidentiality and responsiveness neither side can be; we show that any sound rulebook of n bits omits a compliant program of about n bits.
evidence: Can two rulebooks, one listing what is allowed and one listing what is not, both be complete, if every rule must be backed by evidence that a machine can check in finite time? We prove that they cannot. Checkable evidence can only establish what a finite record settles, and ``never'' and ``eventually'' are never settled by a finite record.
For prohibitions the failure is one-sided: every violation can be caught by watching, but no safe program can be cleared for good. For confidentiality and responsiveness, neither side can be.
We characterise exactly which rules about visible behaviour evidence can confirm, and we show that any sound rulebook of n bits omits a compliant program of about n bits.

highlights.title: Adaptive catalyst discovery emerges from composable scientific intelligence
highlights.authors: Wentao Li, Qilong Cai, Qi Lei et al.
highlights.why: CatAI empirically discovers a pocket catalyst with 9x activity and accelerates photocatalyst optimization, showing composable scientific intelligence can transfer across heterogeneous catalysis tasks.
highlights.key_result: CatAI, a physics-grounded modular AI framework, learns 1.8 million structure-property relations and organizes them into 30 physicochemical encoders, and across benchmark tasks it achieves a 7.8% lower task-averaged prediction error than the next-best models. In experimental validation, CatAI identified a new confined-passable pocket catalyst with 9 times the activity of the commercial benchmark and guided autonomous closed-loop optimization of a highly active Cu-based geminal-atom photocatalyst for C-O coupling reactions surpassing the traditional Ni-based systems.
evidence: To overcome this challenge, we present Composable Catalytic Intelligence (CatAI), a physics-grounded modular AI framework that learns 1.8 million structure-property relations and organizes them into 30 physicochemical encoders.
Across benchmark tasks, CatAI achieves a 7.8% lower task-averaged prediction error than the next-best models.

In experimental validation, CatAI identified a new confined-passable pocket catalyst applicable in industrial homogeneous polymer synthesis with 9 times the activity of the commercial benchmark. In parallel, it guided autonomous closed-loop optimization of a highly active Cu-based geminal-atom photocatalyst for C-O coupling reactions surpassing the traditional Ni-based systems.

highlights.title: Massive Activations Confound Sparse Autoencoders
highlights.why: It shows massive activations dominate SAE variance and corrupt feature interpretability, and the PC1-removal correction substantially improves feature sharing and reconstruction, a crucial methodological fix.
highlights.key_result: Massive activations undermine both variance-explained and ablation-damage evaluations of SAEs. A PC1-bypass correction raises top-50 feature sharing from 4--39.5% to 73--99.5% in affected models; at the same TopK sparsity, the resulting SAE degrades the model up to 44% less and reduces content reconstruction error by up to 33.9%.
evidence: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are commonly evaluated by variance explained and ablation damage. We show how massive activations undermine both evaluations, and propose a correction.
We bypass PC1 by training the SAE on activations with PC1 removed, then adding PC1 to the reconstruction. In affected models, the top-50 feature sharing rate rises from 4--39.5% to 73--99.5%.
At the same TopK sparsity, the resulting SAE degrades the model up to 44% less and reduces content reconstruction error by up to 33.9%.

highlights.title: An evidence-traceable benchmark of clinical reasoning in large language models
highlights.authors: Zhiqun Zhao, Xiaodong Yang, Bruce Gu et al.
highlights.why: Med Evidence Bench ties every criterion to versioned source text and reveals large gaps between guideline recall and patient-specific evidence use, with physician-level grading agreement.
highlights.key_result: Here we developed Med Evidence Bench (MEB; https://www.medevidencebench.org.cn/), comprising 1,536 physician-constructed items across three levels: guideline knowledge, standardized clinical scenarios and real-world laboratory scenarios. Across ten LLMs, the Evidence Trace Score (ETS) was 0.975-0.997 for guideline knowledge, 0.292-0.658 for standardized scenarios and 0.182-0.447 for real-world scenarios, and rankings varied across levels.

Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
news.summary: Google DeepMind made Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists and consumers via the API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, the same introductory price as Gemini 4 Argon. The company reports Carbon ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity's WANDR and Zapier's AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task than the next best external model, ranks #2 on the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark at over 6X lower average cost per task, and is previewing a /swarm multi-agent feature in Google Antigravity.

news.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
news.summary: Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, a multi-LLM agentic framework that formally verified key security properties of the Signal protocol's compiled code, with agents powered by Gemini Carbon generating over six million lines of Lean. The verification took four weeks and needed human review of about one percent of the codebase, and when two previously fixed bugs were reintroduced into an isolated version, the system produced machine-checked proofs that the buggy versions were insecure.

news.title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
news.summary: Google announced new Gemini Intelligence features and expanded device support, including Motorola's first such device, the motorola signature 27 (U.S. pre-order November 19), and Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro XL and Pixel 10 Pro Fold via a Pixel Drop. Rambler 4 arrives on those devices, task automation expands to the UK, India and Japan, and Create My Widget and Device Assistance roll out, with Create My Widget also coming to Pixel Watch in the next few weeks.

news.title: We’re bringing Adobe’s creative and productivity tools closer to your everyday Google apps.
news.summary: At Adobe MAX, Google announced an expanded Adobe partnership bringing Adobe tools into Google products and Google's frontier models into Adobe apps, including an "Edit with" entry point from Drive and Gmail into Acrobat and Acrobat and creative-tool connectors in Gemini and Gemini Enterprise. Adobe's CX Enterprise Coworker agent will be usable in Gemini Enterprise, Adobe creative tools come to AI Mode in Search, and Adobe and Google DeepMind will explore an image model for Photoshop enabling near-real-time edits.

news.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
news.summary: Google Cloud announced Gemini for healthcare, a solution that unifies clinical, operational and administrative data from electronic health records, billing platforms, clinical guidelines and Medicare datasets to execute multi-step workflows such as medical records synthesis and prior authorization review under human oversight. It is initially available in preview with launch partners HCA Healthcare, Highmark Health and Northwell Health, aimed at the nearly 28 hours per week clinicians lose to paperwork and administrative tasks.

news.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
news.summary: Microsoft researchers described "Lazarus," a backdoor technique that reprograms fewer than 10 dormant neurons in a model without retraining, causing an agent to execute attacker commands when a hidden trigger appears (for example, a date change past midnight into 2027) while still passing standard safety evaluations. Microsoft says Foundry verifies model provenance and scans the software environment, and it is developing AI-powered weight scanning, red-teaming tools and cryptographic model signing as defenses.

news.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
news.summary: At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, NVIDIA contributed its OpenShell agent security and governance runtime to the CNCF as a Sandbox project and contributed to Google-led Agent Substrate, also a CNCF Sandbox project, with OpenShell reported to have received tens of thousands of contributions in less than a year since launch. NVIDIA also announced three new DSX AI Factory Platform components: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine, NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot.

news.title: Running AV Reasoning Models Within Onboard Compute and Latency Limits
news.summary: NVIDIA introduced Alpamayo 2 Edge, a 2B-parameter adaptive reasoning vision-language-action model built on the 2B Nemotron-based reasoning backbone of Cosmos 3 Edge, designed for real-time operation on DRIVE AGX Thor and generating Chain-of-Causation reasoning only when needed. Closed-loop reinforcement learning in AlpaGym improved driving performance by 48.9% over the best checkpoint without closed-loop RL, and deployment recipes with TensorRT and DFlash2 achieve 160-190 ms pixel-to-trajectory latency on DRIVE AGX Thor.

news.title: Agent Substrate: Advancing Kubernetes for Agents at Scale
news.summary: Agent Substrate, an open-source zero-trust runtime now in the CNCF Sandbox, multiplexes many agent sessions over a small pool of warm Kubernetes worker Pods, checkpointing idle sessions with full memory and filesystem state and restoring them onto free workers, which NVIDIA says gives 10x higher density than standard containers. It pairs with NVIDIA Dynamo for inference coordination and KAI Scheduler for placement within the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform.

news.title: Start and Restore GPU Workloads in Seconds with NVIDIA Snapshot
news.summary: NVIDIA released Snapshot, an open-source checkpoint and restore system for GPU workloads on Kubernetes that captures fully initialized CPU and GPU memory state and restores it in 3.6 to 42.7 seconds across tested configurations, an 8x to 36x speedup over cold starts. Checkpoint creation takes 15 seconds to 5.5 minutes depending on model size, and the system supports multi-GPU workloads with checkpoints up to 1 TB across eight GPUs; benchmarks used NVIDIA B200 GPUs with VAST NFS storage.

news.title: Manage Kubernetes Clusters for GPU Infrastructure with NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine
news.summary: NVIDIA announced NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR), open-source projects for building and operating managed Kubernetes services on GPU infrastructure, with NVKE managing clusters via a REST API and controllers and NVKR producing version-pinned node images, container images and packages. Both are in public preview under the Apache 2.0 license, not yet recommended for production, with Firmus and SK Telecom integrating them and partners including Mirantis, Rafay, Spectro Cloud, OpenNebula Systems, vCluster and Netris incorporating components.

news.title: Build a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search
news.summary: AWS announced the Web Search API in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now available, returning current results from an Amazon-operated index with each result including title, URL, publication date and an extract, plus domain include/exclude and publication date range filters, with requests signed using existing AWS credentials (SigV4) and no search API key. In the example daily dependency watch built with LangGraph, three research branches finished in 36 seconds versus 99 seconds run one after another, with date window, blocklist and a limit of four searches per branch enforced in code.

news.title: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
news.summary: AWS described agent evaluation on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations using three evaluator sources: AWS-authored built-in evaluators referenced by ID (Builtin.GoalSuccessRate, Builtin.Helpfulness and 13 more), third-party managed evaluators from DeepEval and AutoEval hosted and run by AgentCore, and custom evaluators that modify a built-in or third-party base. The post recommends defining business outcomes, breaking them into observable behaviors, and mapping each to trace-level or session-level evaluators.

news.title: Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
news.summary: Trovata described autonomous treasury agents built on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, with role-based access control and direct connections to over 10,000 banks, moving from its 2023 generative AI for treasury to persistent agentic workflows. Reported customer results include $1M+ in annualized cost savings, over 5 hours per day saved per accounting team, a 77 percent reduction in annual TMS costs and treasury reporting reduced from hours or days to under a minute.

news.title: How TCS built an agentic test orchestrator with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: Tata Consultancy Services described an agentic test orchestrator for Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance clients built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime with the Strands Agents SDK, using specialized agents with a deterministic supervisor and an execution workflow, and choosing AgentCore for model choice, runtime scaling and per-session isolated microVMs for tenant separation. The platform runs five stages with inputs from Jira, business requirement documents and GitLab, hosted on Amazon EKS behind Amazon CloudFront with Amazon Cognito sign-in.

highlights.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
highlights.why: 这种利润与校准感知的重新评估推翻了之前关于 TFM 在客户流失预测上决定性优于 GBDT 的说法，表明仅在调参后的部分数据集上具有细微显著性，从而为当前 TFM 的热潮降温。
highlights.key_result: 在20个预先声明的比较上使用 split-aware 检验和 Holm 校正后，TabPFN-3.5 在 Cell2Cell（1.9%）和 Iranian（7.6%）上获得的 EMP 显著高于最佳调参 GBDT，且这两个增益在分别与三个调参 GBDT 比较时也成立；在 Orange 上它在所有10个划分中领先（14.3%），但校正后增益不显著（Holm p = 0.155）。
evidence: With a split-aware test and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparisons, TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more EMP than the best tuned GBDT on Cell2Cell (1.9%) and Iranian (7.6%), and these two gains also hold against each of the three tuned GBDTs separately.
On Orange it is ahead in all 10 splits (14.3%), but the gain is not significant after correction (Holm p = 0.155).

highlights.title: How Much of Your VLA Is kNN
highlights.authors: Denis Grachev, Damien LaRocque, Omar Moured
highlights.why: kNN 检索基线在 LIBERO 和 LAC 赛道上达到 91.7%，而微调仅改进了键，这质疑了 VLA 是否真正泛化到演示之外，并提示了一个用于评估的低成本基线。
highlights.key_result: 论文表明，检索邻近演示并复用其动作片段，在 LIBERO 上无需策略训练即可达到 91.7 的成功率；在 LIBERO-Plus 扰动下，检索方法在所有被评估策略中下降幅度最小；微调主要使视觉-语言主干成为更好的检索键，而 VLA 的动作仍接近演示。
evidence: In this work, we show that retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks achieves a success rate of 91.7 on LIBERO without policy training. Under LIBERO-Plus perturbations, retrieval shows the smallest drop of all evaluated policies.
Across nine publicly available VLA, fine-tuning mostly makes the vision-language backbone a better retrieval key, and the actions of the VLA remain close to the demonstrations.

On average, the ResNet variant achieves a success rate of 88.7 on LIBERO and 75.5 on LIBERO-Plus. The multimodal variant reaches 91.7 and 82.4 , respectively, while the LAC key variant reaches 93.0 and 81.7 .

highlights.title: ExpertCrowd-SWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Expert-Authored Engineering Tasks in Unfamiliar Codebases
highlights.authors: Josip Vrdoljak, Akash Singh, Bas Steunebrink et al.
highlights.theme: Agentic LLMs, memory, and tool use
highlights.why: ExpertCrowd-SWE 提供了由专家编写、经过校准、在陌生代码库中采用部分给分评分的任务，相比合成或熟悉的代码库，为前沿代理提供了更真实的基准。
highlights.key_result: 在 EC-SWE 上，七个当前模型跨越 35 个百分点的分数范围，并分为四个统计上显著不同的层级；Claude Opus 5.5（67.3%）和 GPT-6 Astra（63.7%）领先，但二者之间没有统计显著差距。没有任何任务被所有模型完全解决，并且在 80 个任务中，没有模型在全部五次运行中获得满分。
evidence: On EC-SWE, seven current models span 35 points and fall into four statistically distinct tiers.

Claude Opus 5.5 (67.3%) and GPT-6 Astra (63.7%) lead without a statistically significant gap, followed by Claude Fable 5.1 (46.5%), Gemini 3.8 Flash (40.0%), and a statistically indistinguishable group of Qwen 3.8 Max, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Grok 4.6 (32-34%).
No task is fully solved by every model, and on 80 tasks no model earns full credit on all five runs.

highlights.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
highlights.authors: Yikun Zhang, Minghao Guo, Guangxue Xu et al.
highlights.why: ProTEUS 学习了一个突变分辨的世界模型，具有快速的物理有效结构预测和闭环反馈，超越了既有模型，并实现了对组合蛋白质空间的高效探索。
highlights.key_result: ProTEUS 在零样本和监督微调的突变预测任务上均超越了既有模型。我们通过实验在醛脱氢酶和果聚糖蔗糖酶上开展了两个闭环多目标工程活动，获得了活性比野生型高 >10 fold 的变体。
evidence: ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type.

highlights.title: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents
highlights.why: 这一不可能性定理形式化地证明，任何有限、可检查的规则手册都无法认证每一个安全程序，为 AI 守门人提供了根本性限制。
highlights.key_result: 我们证明，如果每条规则都必须有机器能在有限时间内检查的证据支持，那么两本规则手册——一本列出允许事项、一本列出禁止事项——不可能同时完备：可检查证据只能确立有限记录所确定的事实，而“never”和“eventually”永远无法由有限记录确定。对于禁止性规则，失效是单侧的——通过监视可以抓住每个违规，但任何安全程序都无法被永久放行；对于机密性和响应性，两侧都无法做到；我们证明，任何 n 比特的健全规则手册都会遗漏大约 n 比特的合规程序。
evidence: Can two rulebooks, one listing what is allowed and one listing what is not, both be complete, if every rule must be backed by evidence that a machine can check in finite time? We prove that they cannot. Checkable evidence can only establish what a finite record settles, and ``never'' and ``eventually'' are never settled by a finite record.
For prohibitions the failure is one-sided: every violation can be caught by watching, but no safe program can be cleared for good. For confidentiality and responsiveness, neither side can be.
We characterise exactly which rules about visible behaviour evidence can confirm, and we show that any sound rulebook of n bits omits a compliant program of about n bits.

highlights.title: Adaptive catalyst discovery emerges from composable scientific intelligence
highlights.authors: Wentao Li, Qilong Cai, Qi Lei et al.
highlights.why: CatAI 通过实验发现了一种活性为 9x 的口袋催化剂，并加速了光催化剂优化，表明可组合的科学智能能够跨异构催化任务迁移。
highlights.key_result: CatAI 是一个基于物理的模块化 AI 框架，学习了 1.8 million 条结构-性质关系，并将它们组织为 30 个物理化学编码器；在基准任务中，其任务平均预测误差比次优模型低 7.8%。在实验验证中，CatAI 发现了一种新的可进入限域口袋催化剂，其活性是商业基准的 9 倍，并引导了对高活性 Cu 基孪生原子光催化剂的自主闭环优化，用于 C-O 偶联反应，超越了传统 Ni 基体系。
evidence: To overcome this challenge, we present Composable Catalytic Intelligence (CatAI), a physics-grounded modular AI framework that learns 1.8 million structure-property relations and organizes them into 30 physicochemical encoders.
Across benchmark tasks, CatAI achieves a 7.8% lower task-averaged prediction error than the next-best models.

In experimental validation, CatAI identified a new confined-passable pocket catalyst applicable in industrial homogeneous polymer synthesis with 9 times the activity of the commercial benchmark. In parallel, it guided autonomous closed-loop optimization of a highly active Cu-based geminal-atom photocatalyst for C-O coupling reactions surpassing the traditional Ni-based systems.

highlights.title: Massive Activations Confound Sparse Autoencoders
highlights.why: 该工作表明，大规模激活主导了 SAE 方差并破坏了特征可解释性，而 PC1 去除校正显著改善了特征共享和重建，是一项关键的方法学修正。
highlights.key_result: 大规模激活削弱了对 SAE 的方差解释和消融损伤评估。PC1 绕过校正将受影响模型中 top-50 特征共享从 4--39.5% 提高到 73--99.5%；在相同 TopK 稀疏度下，所得 SAE 对模型的性能下降减少最多 44%，并将内容重建误差降低最多 33.9%。
evidence: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are commonly evaluated by variance explained and ablation damage. We show how massive activations undermine both evaluations, and propose a correction.
We bypass PC1 by training the SAE on activations with PC1 removed, then adding PC1 to the reconstruction. In affected models, the top-50 feature sharing rate rises from 4--39.5% to 73--99.5%.
At the same TopK sparsity, the resulting SAE degrades the model up to 44% less and reduces content reconstruction error by up to 33.9%.

highlights.title: An evidence-traceable benchmark of clinical reasoning in large language models
highlights.authors: Zhiqun Zhao, Xiaodong Yang, Bruce Gu et al.
highlights.why: Med Evidence Bench 将每项标准与版本化源文本绑定，并揭示了指南召回与患者特异性证据使用之间的巨大差距，同时具有医生级别的评分一致性。
highlights.key_result: 在此，我们开发了 Med Evidence Bench（MEB；https://www.medevidencebench.org.cn/），包含 1,536 个由医生构建的条目，覆盖三个层级：指南知识、标准化临床场景和真实世界实验室场景。在十个 LLM 上，证据追溯得分（ETS）在指南知识上为 0.975-0.997，在标准化场景上为 0.292-0.658，在真实世界场景上为 0.182-0.447，且各层级排名有所不同。
evidence: Here we developed Med Evidence Bench (MEB; https://www.medevidencebench.org.cn/), comprising 1,536 physician-constructed items across three levels: guideline knowledge, standardized clinical scenarios and real-world laboratory scenarios. Each criterion stating a medical claim is linked to a versioned source-text span. Across ten LLMs, the Evidence Trace Score (ETS) was 0.975-0.997 for guideline knowledge, 0.292-0.658 for standardized scenarios and 0.182-0.447 for real-world scenarios, and rankings varied across levels.

news.summary: Google DeepMind 通过 Google AI Studio 中的 API 以及 Gemini for business 向开发者、企业、科学家和消费者提供 Gemini 4 Carbon，价格为每百万输入 token $2、每百万输出 token $10，与 Gemini 4 Argon 的初始价格相同。该公司报告称，Carbon 在 CursorBench 4.0、Perplexity 的 WANDR 和 Zapier 的 AutomationBench 上排名 #1，每任务成本比次佳外部模型低 2X 以上；在新的 Multimodal Knowledge Agent 基准上排名 #2，平均每任务成本低 6X 以上；并正在 Google Antigravity 中预览 /swarm 多智能体功能。

news.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
news.summary: Google DeepMind 推出了 AlphaProof Code，这是一个多 LLM 智能体框架，正式验证了 Signal 协议编译代码的关键安全性质；由 Gemini Carbon 驱动的智能体生成了超过 six million 行 Lean。验证耗时 four weeks，需要人工审查约 one percent 的代码库；当将两个之前已修复的 bug 重新引入隔离版本时，系统生成了机器可检查的证明，表明这些有缺陷的版本是不安全的。

news.title: Gemini Intelligence: New features, on more devices
news.summary: Google announced new Gemini Intelligence features and expanded device support, including Motorola's first such device, the motorola signature 27 (U.S. pre-order November 19), and Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro XL and Pixel 10 Pro Fold via a Pixel Drop. Rambler 4 arrives on those devices, task automation expands to the UK, India and Japan, and Create My Widget and Device Assistance roll out, with Create My Widget also coming to Pixel Watch in the next few weeks.

news.title: We’re bringing Adobe’s creative and productivity tools closer to your everyday Google apps.
news.summary: 在 Adobe MAX 上，Google 宣布扩大与 Adobe 的合作，将 Adobe 工具引入 Google 产品，并将 Google 的前沿模型引入 Adobe 应用，包括从 Drive 和 Gmail 进入 Acrobat 的“Edit with”入口，以及 Gemini 和 Gemini Enterprise 中的 Acrobat 和创意工具连接器。Adobe 的 CX Enterprise Coworker 智能体将可在 Gemini Enterprise 中使用，Adobe 创意工具将进入 Search 中的 AI Mode，Adobe 与 Google DeepMind 将探索用于 Photoshop 的图像模型，以实现近实时编辑。

news.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
news.summary: Google Cloud 发布了 Gemini for healthcare，这是一个将来自电子健康记录、计费平台、临床指南和 Medicare 数据集的临床、运营和行政数据统一起来的解决方案，可在人工监督下执行多步骤工作流，如病历综合和预授权审查。它最初以预览版提供，启动合作伙伴包括 HCA Healthcare、Highmark Health 和 Northwell Health，旨在解决临床医生每周因文书和行政工作损失近 28 小时的问题。

news.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
news.summary: 微软研究人员描述了一种名为“Lazarus”的后门技术，该技术在不重新训练的情况下重编程模型中不到 10 个休眠神经元，当隐藏触发器出现时（例如日期跨过午夜进入 2027 年），诱使智能体执行攻击者命令，同时仍能通过标准安全评估。微软表示，Foundry 会验证模型来源并扫描软件环境，且正在开发 AI 驱动的权重扫描、红队工具和加密模型签名作为防御手段。

news.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
news.summary: 在 KubeCon + CloudNativeCon 上，NVIDIA 将其 OpenShell 智能体安全与治理运行时贡献给 CNCF 作为 Sandbox 项目，并参与由 Google 主导的 Agent Substrate（也是一个 CNCF Sandbox 项目）；据报道，OpenShell 自发布不到一年已收到数万次贡献。NVIDIA 还发布了三个新的 DSX AI Factory Platform 组件：NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine、NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes 和 NVIDIA Snapshot。

news.title: Running AV Reasoning Models Within Onboard Compute and Latency Limits
news.summary: NVIDIA 推出了 Alpamayo 2 Edge，这是一个 2B 参数的自适应推理视觉-语言-动作模型，构建在 Cosmos 3 Edge 的 2B Nemotron 推理主干上，旨在 DRIVE AGX Thor 上实时运行，并仅在需要时生成 Chain-of-Causation 推理。在 AlpaGym 中进行闭环强化学习后，驾驶性能比未使用闭环 RL 的最佳检查点提高了 48.9%；配合 TensorRT 和 DFlash2 的部署方案在 DRIVE AGX Thor 上实现了 160-190 ms 的像素到轨迹延迟。

news.title: Agent Substrate: Advancing Kubernetes for Agents at Scale
news.summary: Agent Substrate 是一个现已进入 CNCF Sandbox 的开源零信任运行时，它将大量智能体会话多路复用在一小池热 Kubernetes 工作 Pod 上，对空闲会话进行完整内存和文件系统状态的检查点保存，并在空闲工作节点上恢复；NVIDIA 称这比标准容器提供了 10x 更高的密度。它与 NVIDIA Dynamo 配合进行推理协调，并与 KAI Scheduler 配合在 NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform 内进行调度。

news.title: Start and Restore GPU Workloads in Seconds with NVIDIA Snapshot
news.summary: NVIDIA 发布了 Snapshot，这是一个用于 Kubernetes 上 GPU 工作负载的开源检查点与恢复系统，可捕获完全初始化的 CPU 和 GPU 内存状态，并在测试配置中在 3.6 到 42.7 秒内恢复，相比冷启动实现了 8x 到 36x 的加速。检查点创建时间根据模型大小从 15 秒到 5.5 分钟不等；该系统支持跨八个 GPU 的多 GPU 工作负载，检查点最大可达 1 TB；基准测试使用了 NVIDIA B200 GPU 和 VAST NFS 存储。

news.title: Manage Kubernetes Clusters for GPU Infrastructure with NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine
news.summary: NVIDIA 发布了 NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine（NVKE）和 NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes（NVKR），这两个开源项目用于在 GPU 基础设施上构建和运营托管 Kubernetes 服务；NVKE 通过 REST API 和控制器管理集群，NVKR 生成版本固定的节点镜像、容器镜像和软件包。两者均以 Apache 2.0 许可证提供公开预览，尚未建议用于生产环境；Firmus 和 SK Telecom 正在集成它们，Mirantis、Rafay、Spectro Cloud、OpenNebula Systems、vCluster 和 Netris 等合作伙伴正在纳入相关组件。

news.title: Build a daily dependency watcher with LangGraph and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search
news.summary: AWS 宣布 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 中的 Web Search API 现已可用，可从 Amazon 运营的索引返回当前结果，每个结果包含标题、URL、发布日期和摘要，并提供域名包含/排除和发布日期范围过滤器；请求使用现有 AWS 凭证（SigV4）签名，无需搜索 API 密钥。在使用 LangGraph 构建的每日依赖监控示例中，三个研究分支在 36 秒内完成，而顺序运行需要 99 秒；代码中强制实施了日期窗口、黑名单以及每个分支最多四次搜索的限制。

news.title: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
news.summary: AWS 描述了在 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations 上进行智能体评估的三种评估器来源：由 AWS 编写并通过 ID 引用的内置评估器（Builtin.GoalSuccessRate、Builtin.Helpfulness 以及另外 13 个）、由 AgentCore 托管和运行的来自 DeepEval 和 AutoEval 的第三方托管评估器，以及修改内置或第三方基础的自定义评估器。文章建议定义业务成果，将其分解为可观察行为，并将每个行为映射到 trace 级或 session 级评估器。

news.title: Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
news.summary: Trovata 描述了基于 Amazon Bedrock 和 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 构建的自主财资智能体，具有基于角色的访问控制，并可直连超过 10,000 家银行，从 2023 年的生成式 AI 财资应用转向持久化的智能体工作流。报告的客户成果包括年化成本节省超过 $1M+、每个会计团队每天节省超过 5 小时、年度 TMS 成本降低 77 percent，以及财资报告从数小时或数天缩短到不到一分钟。

news.title: How TCS built an agentic test orchestrator with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
news.summary: Tata Consultancy Services 描述了一个面向银行、金融服务和保险客户的智能体测试编排器，该编排器基于 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 运行时和 Strands Agents SDK 构建，使用具有确定性监督器和执行工作流的专用智能体，并选择 AgentCore 是为了获得模型选择、运行时扩展以及用于租户隔离的每会话隔离 microVM。该平台运行五个阶段，输入来自 Jira、业务需求文档和 GitLab，托管在 Amazon EKS 上，前面有 Amazon CloudFront，并使用 Amazon Cognito 登录。
